title: SLA-aware phased onboarding lanes + compatibility probe for customer model intake
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers frequently request new model variants, version pins, or delayed deprecations. Current intake is ad-hoc, causing inconsistent risk assessments, missed SLAs, and surprise regressions in production. Goal: Build an SLA-aware, phased onboarding lane that automatically assigns requests to one of three acceptance lanes (fast-path for paid SLAs, standard triage, and gated shadowing) and runs a compatibility probe + lightweight eval gate before manual review. This ticket defines scope, acceptance criteria, success metrics, rollout plan, and stakeholder signoffs for a pilot.
proposal_summary: Introduce an intake form extension that captures SLA tier, workload type, canary/sample prompts, and backwards-compatibility constraints. System will run an automated compatibility probe (binary compatibility tests, sample output diff, latency profile) and a lightweight eval against customer-provided prompt sets. Probe results plus SLA weight produce a priority score used to route to: 1) Fast-path (automated onboarding + 24h SLA), 2) Standard (PM review + eval gate), 3) Shadow-gate (staged shadowing with rollback rules). Provide explicit pin-exemption rules and deprecation windows per SLA.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Intake form collects required fields and stores request metadata. 2) Compatibility probe runs automatically and produces a human-readable report stored in ticket. 3) Eval gate runs with pass/fail thresholds and stores metric deltas (accuracy/quality/regression). 4) Routing decision produced deterministically and auditable. 5) Pilot onboarded 5 customer requests across tiers with no critical regressions. 6) Audit trail and KMS-encrypted artifacts available for enterprise review.
success_metrics: - Mean time from request -> routing decision < 48h for standard lane and < 24h for fast-path. - % of automated probes that surface actionable regressions >= 85%. - Reduction in manual triage time by 40%. - Zero P0 regressions for pilot customers over 30 days.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Automated probes may produce false positives on creative prompt distributions; to mitigate, include conservative fail/pass thresholds and human review override. - Adding probes increases compute cost; cap probe budget per request and reuse cached artifacts when possible. - Fast-path speed vs safety: limit fast-path to customers with contracts and verified rollback capability. - Privacy: customer prompt sets must be handled per privacy agreement and optionally run inside a private VPC sandbox.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Intake form + metadata store + compatibility probe prototype (latency + token diffs). Phase 2 (3 weeks): Eval gate integration (lightweight metrics), deterministic routing rules, UI visibility in Console. Phase 3 (2 weeks): Pilot with 5 customers (mix of hosted/dedicated/private). Phase 4: Post-pilot iterate on thresholds and expand rollout. Engineering tasks split into ENG infra (probe runner), ENG runtime (compatibility checks), PM integrations, and Console UX for routing visibility.
